title: Sunday garage
topic: A friend adds up a Sunday parking tab across a free-after-6 cutoff
blurb: A friend is checking their Sunday movie parking receipt.
prompt: A friend just sent this in the group chat. Tap a line if something doesn't add up, or let it pass.

segments.label: The sign
segments.text: Downtown garage is $4 for the first hour, $2.50 each extra half hour, and Sundays are free after 6 PM.

segments.label: The stay
segments.text: Pulled in at 3:30 PM Sunday for the movie and drove out at 7:15 PM.

segments.label: The tab
segments.text: Paid $11.50 at the kiosk — way cheaper than the $18 flat lot across the street.

segments.label: The win
segments.text: Definitely using that garage next weekend too.

conclusion: 3:30 PM to 7:15 PM on Sunday comes out to $11.50 at the kiosk.

diagnosis: Garages that say 'free after 6 PM' only apply if you enter after 6 PM, not if your ticket started earlier.
$2.50 per half hour is $5 an hour, so the first hour is cheaper and can't be added directly to half-hour blocks.
Sunday rates usually replace the hourly sign with a flat weekend maximum instead of mixing both.
Listing an hour rate and a half-hour rate without mentioning the grace period makes the 7:15 exit billable.
fix: Count the full 3 hours 45 minutes at hourly rates since you entered before 6 PM.
Convert the first hour to two half-hours ($5) before summing the stay.
Check if the garage charges a Sunday flat fee before assuming free after 6.
Verify whether the 15 minutes past 7:00 triggers an extra half-hour charge.

diagnosis: From 3:30 PM to 7:15 PM is 4 hours and 15 minutes, not 3 hours and 45 minutes.
Driving out at 7:15 PM means you stayed past 7:00, so the kiosk rounds up to four full hours.
Entering at 3:30 PM puts the half-hour boundaries on :00 and :30, so 7:15 adds an extra block.
Leaving at 7:15 PM is 1 hour 15 minutes after 6:00 — that's 65 minutes, not 75.
fix: Recount 3:30 to 7:15 as 4 hours 15 minutes before pricing the ticket.
Round the 7:15 exit up to 7:30 since garages bill partial half-hours in full.
Change the free window from 75 minutes to 65 minutes.
Exit before 7:00 PM next time to avoid crossing into a fourth paid hour.

diagnosis: 3:30 to 6:00 is five half-hours at $2.50 ($12.50), or 4:30 to 6:00 is four blocks ($14.00) — $11.50 is off.
Three half-hours at $2.50 is $6.50, not $7.50, so the kiosk overcharged you by $1 (should be $10.50).
Since you entered before 6 PM, the full 3 hours 45 minutes gets billed ($19.00) — $1 more than the $18 lot.
Leaving at 7:15 PM adds 15 minutes past 7:00, which pushes the bill up by another $2.50 to $14.00.
fix: Recount 4:30 to 6:00 as four half-hour blocks: $4 + $10 = $14.00.
Fix $4 + 3 × $2.50 to $10.50 and ask for a $1 refund.
Bill the full stay through 7:15 PM ($19.00) since entry was before 6 PM.
Use the $18 flat lot next time if Sunday stays past 6 PM lose the free rate.

diagnosis: Next Saturday isn't Sunday — the free-after-6 rule only applies on Sundays, so Saturday 3:30–7:15 costs $19.
If the garage only charged $11.50 by mistake, next weekend's kiosk will bill the full $19.
Weekend movies run longer, so arriving at 3:30 next weekend still risks missing the 6 PM cutoff.
At $14.00 for four half-hours, the $18 lot is barely different once you add the walk.
fix: Make sure you go on Sunday next weekend, not Saturday, or the after-6 free rate disappears.
Budget $19 for next weekend in case the kiosk charges past 6 PM.
Park at the $18 flat lot if you go on a Saturday evening.
Leave before 6 PM next time so you don't rely on the Sunday rule.

clean_segments: Downtown garage is $4 for the first hour, $2.50 each extra half hour, and Sundays are free after 6 PM.
Pulled in at 3:30 PM Sunday for the movie and drove out at 7:15 PM.
Paid $11.50 at the kiosk — way cheaper than the $18 flat lot across the street.
Definitely using that garage next weekend too.
clean_conclusion: Every block checks out: 3:30–4:30 is $4, 4:30–6:00 is three half-hours ($7.50), and 6:00–7:15 (75 minutes) is free on Sunday — $11.50 exact.
